subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

A formal, written modification or clarification to the solicitation documents issued before the bid opening date

questions.explain: An Addendum (or Amendment) is the only legally binding mechanism used to clarify, correct, or change the contents of a solicitation while it is actively out on the street prior to the due date.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: If a buyer receives a critical, clarifying question from Vendor A regarding ambiguous specs via email, the buyer should:
options: Reply directly to Vendor A so they have an advantage
Call Vendor A to provide an off-the-record explanation
Draft a formal addendum containing the question and answer, and distribute it to all plan-holders/registered vendors
Ignore the question if the answer is difficult
questions.explain: To maintain a level playing field, if an ambiguity is identified by one vendor, the clarification must be distributed to all potential bidders simultaneously via an addendum.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: An agency issues a major addendum completely overhauling the required pricing sheet just 48 hours before the scheduled public bid opening. What is the most appropriate action for the buyer to take?
options: Maintain the original opening date and tell vendors to work quickly
Issue a subsequent addendum extending the bid opening date to give vendors adequate time to adjust their pricing
Accept late bids up to three days after the opening
Permit vendors to submit the old pricing sheet and negotiate later
questions.explain: When a material change is made close to the due date, best practice (and often statute) requires the agency to extend the due date to ensure vendors have sufficient time to formulate accurate, responsible bids.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: During bid evaluation, the buyer notices that the lowest bidder failed to sign or return the acknowledgment of Addendum #1. Addendum #1 added a requirement for a high-cost warranty. How should this be handled?
options: Call the vendor and let them email the acknowledgment
Assume they read it and proceed to award
Deem the bid non-responsive because the unacknowledged addendum materially affected price and liability
Deduct points from their evaluation score
questions.explain: Failing to acknowledge a material addendum (one that impacts price, quantity, quality, or delivery) means the vendor has not agreed to the new terms, rendering their bid non-responsive. Waiving this would give them an unfair pricing advantage over others who included the warranty cost.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: A vendor submits a written question asking for clarification on the packaging requirements. The buyer realizes the answer is already clearly stated on page 14 of the IFB. How should the buyer proceed?
options: Issue an addendum answering the question and pointing to page 14 to ensure all vendors have clarity
Ignore the question since the vendor obviously didn't read the document
Reject the vendor's eventual bid because they showed a lack of understanding
Wait until the pre-bid conference and only mention it if asked again
questions.explain: Even if the answer is already in the document, best practice dictates addressing all formal questions submitted prior to the deadline via an addendum, simply citing the existing section to reinforce clarity and maintain transparency for all potential bidders.
